expl.summary: This formula is fitted without any jet-mass observable: no if-statement tests the jet mass, a subjet mass or mass/pT, so every neuron is built from widths (girth, girth2, width, lam1, LHA), energy correlations (e2, e2_sq, e3), N-subjettiness (tau1, tau2), subjet distances, the total pT and the pT of the hardest particles. Its accuracy on the validation jets is 0.653. Mass information enters only indirectly: neuron 2 falls with jet mass (rank correlation -0.73) and the q score falls with it (-0.741) although mass is never tested, because at fixed pT a wider jet is a heavier jet. The t score is set by jet size: it subtracts the compact-jet neuron 13 (-48%), on which tops sit far below every other class (0.998 against 3.59 to 4.38), and adds the overall-size neuron 10 (+26%), so it follows girth, width and girth2 (rank correlations 0.92 to 0.93). The q and g scores both add the narrow-jet neuron 9 (+55% and +22%); the g score is separated from the q score by neuron 2 (narrow, low-angularity jets at total pT below 831 GeV, +38% in g only) and by neuron 5 (pT concentrated in the few hardest particles), which the g score subtracts (-14%) and the q score adds (+6%). The W and Z scores add the elongated two-prong neuron 7 (+13% and +35%) and subtract the wide-angle radiation neuron 3 and the off-centre neuron 6. W and Z are separated only by widths: the W score adds the compact, centred neuron 11 (+24%), while the intermediate-girth neuron 14, on which Z jets sit highest (1.33 against 0.164 for W jets), is added to the Z score (+6%) and subtracted from the W score (-10%); neuron 15 (girth2 between 0.00749 and 0.0136 with small tau1) takes more out of the W score (-7.5%) than out of the Z score (-2.2%).

2.title: narrow, low-angularity jet at total pT below 831 GeV
